title.zh: 卷四十 志第十: 地理志四
title.raw: 卷四十 志第十: 地理志四 Volume 40 Treatises 10: Geography 4

translations.literal: Geography Treatise IV: Nanjing Circuit
translations.idiomatic: Geography Treatise IV — Nanjing Circuit

sentences.zh: 南京析津府，本古冀州之地。

translations.literal: Nanjing Xijin Prefecture—in ancient times the land of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xijin Prefecture at Nanjing was the old territory of Ji.

sentences.zh: 高陽氏謂之幽陵，陶唐曰幽都，有虞析為幽州。

translations.literal: Gaoyang called it Youling; Taotang Youdu; Shun divided out Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyang era knew it as Youling; Yao as Youdu; Shun carved out Youzhou.

translations.literal: Shang merged You into Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shang, You was folded into Ji.

translations.literal: Zhou divided and rejoined as You.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou reorganized the region once more as You.

sentences.zh: 《職方》，東北幽州，山鎮醫巫閭，澤藪貘養，川河、泲，浸淄、時。

translations.literal: Offices of Region: northeast Youzhou; mountain cult Yiwulü; marsh Mo yang; rivers He, Cuo; soaking Zi, Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Region record northeast Youzhou with cult mountain Yiwulü, marsh Mo yang, rivers He and Cuo, and the Zi and Shi soaking-in lands.

sentences.zh: 其利魚、鹽，其畜馬、牛、豕，其谷黍、稷、稻。

translations.literal: Products fish and salt; livestock horses, cattle, swine; grains millet, panicum, rice.
translations.idiomatic: Its staples were fish and salt; its herds horses, cattle, and pigs; its grains millet, panicum, and rice.

translations.literal: King Wu enfeoffed Grand Guardian Shi in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu enfeoffed the Grand Guardian Shi in Yan.

sentences.zh: 秦以其地為漁陽、上谷、右北平、遼西、遼東五郡。

translations.literal: Qin made the territory five commanderies: Yuyang, Shanggu, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin organized the region into Yuyang, Shanggu, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 漢為燕國，歷封臧荼、盧綰、劉建、劉澤、劉旦，嘗置涿郡廣陽國。

translations.literal: Han made it the State of Yan, successively enfeoffing Zang Tu, Lu Wan, Liu Jian, Liu Ze, Liu Dan; at times Zhuo Commandery and Guangyang State were placed here.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han it became the State of Yan, held in turn by Zang Tu, Lu Wan, Liu Jian, Liu Ze, and Liu Dan, with Zhuo Commandery and Guangyang State established at intervals.

sentences.zh: 後漢為廣平國廣陽郡，或合於上谷，復置幽州。

translations.literal: Later Han made Guangping State and Guangyang Commandery, sometimes merged into Shanggu, then Youzhou was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han assigned Guangping State and Guangyang Commandery, at times joined to Shanggu; Youzhou was set up again.

sentences.zh: 後周置燕及范陽郡，隋為幽州總管。

translations.literal: Later Zhou placed Yan and Fanyang commanderies; Sui made Youzhou a grand protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou created Yan and Fanyang commanderies; Sui made Youzhou a grand protectorate.

sentences.zh: 唐置大都督府，改范陽節度使。

translations.literal: Tang placed a metropolitan grand protectorate and changed it to the Fanyang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tang installed a metropolitan grand protectorate, later the Fanyang military governor.

sentences.zh: 安祿山、史思明、李懷山、朱滔、劉怦、劉濟，相繼割據。

translations.literal: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Cong, Liu Ji seized the region in succession.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Cong, and Liu Ji carved it out one after another.

translations.literal: Liu Zong submitted to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong returned to Tang allegiance.

sentences.zh: 至張仲武、張允仲，以正得民。

translations.literal: Through Zhang Zhongwu and Zhang Yunzhong righteousness won the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Zhongwu and Zhang Yunzhong upright rule won the populace.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭父子僭爭，遂入五代。

translations.literal: Father and son Liu Rengong contended in usurpation, and the region passed into the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong and his son fought in mutual usurpation until the land entered the Five Dynasties era.

sentences.zh: 自唐而晉，高祖以遼有援立之勞，割幽州等十六州以獻。

translations.literal: From Tang into Jin, Gaozu, for Liao aid in enthroning him, ceded Youzhou and fifteen other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang gave way to Jin, Gaozu rewarded Liao for supporting his accession by ceding Youzhou and the other fifteen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太宗升為南京，又曰燕京。

translations.literal: Taizong raised it to Nanjing, also called Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong promoted it to Nanjing, also styled Yanjing.

translations.literal: Changping County.
translations.idiomatic: Changping County.

sentences.zh: 本漢軍都縣，後漢屬廣陽郡，晉屬燕國，元魏置東燕州、平昌郡及昌平縣。

translations.literal: Originally Han Jundu County; Later Han belonged to Guangyang Commandery; Jin to Yan State; Northern Wei set Eastern Yan Prefecture, Pingchang Commandery, and Changping County.
translations.idiomatic: It was Han Jundu County; Later Han Guangyang Commandery; Jin Yan State; Northern Wei founded Eastern Yan Prefecture, Pingchang Commandery, and Changping County.

translations.literal: Commandery abolished; county subordinated to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was abolished the county answered to Youzhou.

translations.literal: Ninety li north of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay ninety li north of the capital.

translations.literal: Seven thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Lu County.
translations.idiomatic: Lu County.

translations.literal: Originally a Han county, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a Han county in Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐武德二年置元州，貞觀元年州廢，復為縣。

translations.literal: Tang Wude year 2 set Yuan Prefecture; Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished and it again became a county.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Wude year 2 created Yuan Prefecture; in Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished and the county restored.

translations.literal: There is the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu River flows there.

translations.literal: Sixty li east of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood sixty li east of the capital.

translations.literal: Six thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Anji County.
translations.idiomatic: Anji County.

translations.literal: Originally a Han county, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a Han county in Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐武德四年徙置東南五十里石梁城，貞觀八年又徙今縣西五里常道城，開元二十三年又徙耿就橋行市南。

translations.literal: Tang Wude year 4 moved fifty li southeast to Shiliang walled town; Zhenguan year 8 again moved five li west of the present county to Changdao walled town; Kaiyuan year 23 again moved south of Gengjiu Bridge market.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Wude year 4 the seat shifted fifty li southeast to Shiliang town; Zhenguan year 8 to Changdao town five li west of the present site; Kaiyuan year 23 to the market south of Gengjiu Bridge.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred twenty li south of the capital.

translations.literal: Twelve thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Yongqing County.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing County.

sentences.zh: 本漢益昌縣，隋置通澤縣，唐置武隆縣，改會昌，天寶初為永清縣。

translations.literal: Originally Han Yichang County; Sui set Tongze County; Tang set Wulong County, renamed Huichang; at the start of Tianbao it became Yongqing County.
translations.idiomatic: It was Han Yichang County; Sui Tongze County; Tang Wulong, then Huichang; at the opening of Tianbao it was renamed Yongqing.

translations.literal: One hundred fifty li south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one hundred fifty li south of the capital.

translations.literal: Five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Wuqing County.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqing County.

translations.literal: Former Han Yongnu County, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han Yongnu County in Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 《水經註》，雍奴者，藪澤之名，四面有水曰雍，不流曰奴。

translations.literal: Commentary on the Water Classic: Yongnu is the name of a marsh-lake; water on four sides is yong; water that does not flow is nu.
translations.idiomatic: The Water Classic commentary explains Yongnu as a marsh name: water on four sides is yong; stagnant water is nu.

translations.literal: At the start of Tang Tianbao it was changed to Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tang Tianbao it was renamed Wuqing.

translations.literal: One hundred fifty li southeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred fifty li southeast of the capital.

translations.literal: Ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Xianghe County.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghe County.

translations.literal: Originally Sun Village in Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Sun Village in Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 遼於新倉置榷鹽院，居民聚集，因分武清、三河、潞三縣戶置。

translations.literal: Liao placed a salt monopoly office at Xincang; residents gathered; households were split from Wuqing, Sanhe, and Lu counties to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao founded a salt monopoly at Xincang; settlers clustered there, and households were carved from Wuqing, Sanhe, and Lu to form the county.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li southeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one hundred twenty li southeast of the capital.

translations.literal: Seven thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Yuhe County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhe County.

translations.literal: Originally Quanshan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Quanshan land.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭於大安山創宮觀，師煉丹羽化之術於方士王若訥，因割薊縣分置，以供給之。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong built palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; the master Wang Ruone taught elixir and ascension arts to the court; Jixian was split off to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong erected palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; Wang Ruone instructed the court in alchemy; a portion of Jixian was detached to provision them.

translations.literal: Forty li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay forty li west of the capital.

translations.literal: One thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Huoyin County.
translations.idiomatic: Huoyin County.

translations.literal: Originally Huo Village in Han Quanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Huo Village in Han Quanshan.

sentences.zh: 遼每季春，弋獵於延芳澱，居民成邑，就城故漷陰鎮，後改為縣。

translations.literal: Each spring Liao hunted at Yanfang Marsh; residents formed a town; the old Huoyin walled town was walled, later changed to a county.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring the Liao hunted at Yanfang Marsh; settlers formed a town around the old Huoyin fort, later raised to a county.

translations.literal: Ninety li southeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood ninety li southeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 延芳澱方數百里，春時鵝鶩所聚，夏秋多菱芡。

translations.literal: Yanfang Marsh spans several hundred li; in spring geese and ducks gather; in summer and autumn many water chestnuts and lotus roots grow.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfang Marsh covers hundreds of li; spring brings geese and ducks; summer and autumn yield water chestnuts and lotus.

sentences.zh: 國主春獵，衛士皆衣墨綠，各持連鎚、鷹食、刺鵝錐，列水次，相去五七步。

translations.literal: When the ruler hunted in spring, guards all wore dark green, each holding linked maces, hawk food, and goose-stabbing awls, lined along the water five or seven paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: For the spring hunt guards wore dark green, spaced five or seven paces along the shore with linked maces, hawk bait, and goose awls.

sentences.zh: 上風擊鼓，驚鵝稍離水面。

translations.literal: Upwind they beat drums to startle geese slightly from the water.
translations.idiomatic: Drums upwind startled geese to lift slightly from the water.

sentences.zh: 國主親放海東青鶻擒之。

translations.literal: The ruler personally loosed eastern-sea green goshawks to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler himself flew eastern-sea green goshawks to take them.

sentences.zh: 鵝墜，恐鶻力不勝，在列者以佩錐刺鵝，急取其臘飼鶻。

translations.literal: When a goose fell, fearing the hawk lacked strength, those in line stabbed the goose with belt awls and swiftly took its fat to feed the hawk.
translations.idiomatic: If a goose fell and the hawk might fail, men in line stabbed it with belt awls and hurriedly took its fat for the hawk.

translations.literal: Whoever took the lead goose received silver and silk by rule.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing the lead goose brought a standard reward of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 國主、皇族、群臣各有分地。

translations.literal: Ruler, imperial clan, and ministers each had allotted grounds.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler, imperial kin, and ministers each held assigned hunting grounds.

translations.literal: Five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

sentences.zh: 宋王曾《上契丹事》曰：「自雄州白溝驛渡河，四十里至新城縣，古督亢亭之地。

translations.literal: Song minister Wang Zeng, Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan, says: "From Xiongzhou Baima post one crosses the river; forty li to Xincheng County, ancient Dukang Pavilion ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: "From Xiongzhou's Baima post, forty li by ferry to Xincheng County, the old Dukang Pavilion site.

translations.literal: Another seventy li to Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy li farther on lies Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 北渡範水、劉李河，六十里至良鄉縣。

translations.literal: Northward crossing Fan River and Liu-Li River, sixty li to Liangxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Fan and Liu-Li rivers northward, sixty li to Liangxiang County.

sentences.zh: 渡盧溝河，六十里至幽州，號燕京。

translations.literal: Crossing Lugou River, sixty li to Youzhou, styled Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty li beyond the Lugou River stands Youzhou, called Yanjing.

translations.literal: The inner city was built against the outer wall's southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The inner city hugged the southwest of the outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 正南曰啟夏門，內有元和殿，東門曰宣和。

translations.literal: Due south is Qixia Gate; within is Yuanhe Hall; east gate is Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: The south gate is Qixia; inside stands Yuanhe Hall; the east gate is Xuanhe.

translations.literal: Within the city every ward lane had towers.
translations.idiomatic: Every ward and lane in the city had gate-towers.

sentences.zh: 有閔忠寺，本唐太宗為征遼陣亡將士所造；

translations.literal: There is Minzhong Temple, originally built by Tang Taizong for generals and soldiers who died campaigning against Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong Temple, which Tang Taizong raised for officers and men fallen on the Liaodong campaign;

sentences.zh: 又有開泰寺，魏王耶律漢寧造。

translations.literal: also Kaitai Temple, built by Prince of Wei Yelü Hanning.
translations.idiomatic: and Kaitai Temple, built by Prince of Wei Yelü Hanning.

translations.literal: Both were sent envoys from the court to visit.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys were sent to tour both.

sentences.zh: 南門外有於越王廨，為宴集之所。

translations.literal: Outside the south gate is the Prince of Yu Wang's office, a place for banquets.
translations.idiomatic: South of the gate stands the Prince of Yu's hall, used for feasts.

sentences.zh: 門外永平館，舊名碣石館，請和後易之。

translations.literal: Outside the gate is Yongping Hostel, formerly named Jieshi Hostel, renamed after the peace treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the gate is Yongping Hostel, formerly Jieshi Hostel, renamed after the peace accord.

translations.literal: South of it is the Sanggan River.
translations.idiomatic: South lies the Sanggan River.

translations.literal: Shun Prefecture, Guihua Army, middle grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Shun Prefecture—Guihua Army, middle grade, with a prefect.

sentences.zh: 秦上谷，漢范陽，北齊歸德郡境。

translations.literal: Qin Shanggu; Han Fanyang; Northern Qi Guidde Commandery territory.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin it was Shanggu; in Han Fanyang; in Northern Qi part of Guidde Commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，粟末靺鞨與高麗戰不勝，厥稽部長突地稽率八部勝兵數千人，自扶餘城西北舉落內附，置順州以處之。

translations.literal: Sui Kaihuang era: Sumo Mohe fought Goryeo without victory; chief Tudi of the Jueji tribe led several thousand victorious warriors of eight tribes from northwest of Fuyu walled city to submit inward; Shun Prefecture was set to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang, Sumo Mohe lost to Goryeo; Jueji chief Tudi led several thousand warriors of eight tribes from northwest of Fuyu to submit, and Shun Prefecture was founded to receive them.

sentences.zh: 唐武德初改燕州，會昌中改歸順州，唐末仍為順州。

translations.literal: Tang early Wude changed it to Yan Prefecture; Huichang era changed to Guishun Prefecture; late Tang it remained Shun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang Wude renamed it Yan Prefecture; in Huichang it became Guishun; by late Tang it was again Shun Prefecture.

translations.literal: There are Wanyu River and Baisui River;
translations.idiomatic: It has the Wanyu and Baisui rivers;

sentences.zh: 曹王山，曹操嘗駐軍於此，黍谷山，鄒衍吹律之地，南有齊長城。

translations.literal: Caowang Mountain, where Cao Cao once encamped; Taigu Valley, where Zou Yan blew the pitch pipes; south of it is Qi's Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Caowang Mountain, where Cao Cao once camped; Taigu Valley, where Zou Yan tested pitch pipes; to the south runs Qi's Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 城東北有華林、天柱二莊，遼建涼殿，春賞花，夏納涼。

translations.literal: Northeast of the city are Hualin and Tianzhu two estates; Liao built cool halls—spring for flowers, summer for shade.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the city stand the Hualin and Tianzhu estates; the Liao built cool pavilions for spring blossoms and summer shade.

translations.literal: At first the army was called Guining; later renamed.
translations.idiomatic: The army was first called Guining, then renamed.

translations.literal: Governing one county:
translations.idiomatic: It governed one county:

translations.literal: Huairou County.
translations.idiomatic: Huairou County.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀六年置，治五柳城，改順義縣。

translations.literal: Tang Zhenguan year 6 established, administering Wuliu walled town, renamed Shunyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Tang Zhenguan year 6 at Wuliu town, renamed Shunyi County.

sentences.zh: 開元四年置松漠府彈汗州。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan year 4 set Songmo Protectorate Tanhan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 4 placed Songmo Protectorate's Tanhan Prefecture here.

translations.literal: Kaibao year 1 changed to Guihua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kaibao year 1 it became Guihua Commandery.

translations.literal: Qianyuan year 1 restored the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan year 1 restored the current name.

translations.literal: Five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Miyun County.
translations.idiomatic: Miyun County.

sentences.zh: 本漢白檀縣，後漢以居斤奚。

translations.literal: Originally Han Baitan County; Later Han assigned the Jijin Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Baitan County; Later Han placed the Jijin Xi there.

sentences.zh: 元魏置密雲郡，領白檀、要陽、密雲三縣。

translations.literal: Northern Wei set Miyun Commandery, governing Baitan, Yaoyang, and Miyun three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei founded Miyun Commandery over Baitan, Yaoyang, and Miyun counties.

translations.literal: Northern Qi abolished the commandery and two counties; they came under this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi abolished the commandery and two counties, which then belonged here.

translations.literal: Five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Xingtang County.
translations.idiomatic: Xingtang County.

translations.literal: Originally Ding Prefecture Xingtang County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Xingtang County in Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖掠定州，破行唐，盡驅其民，北至檀州，擇曠土居之，凡置十寨，仍名行唐縣。

translations.literal: Taizu raided Ding Prefecture, broke Xingtang, and drove all its people north to Tan Prefecture, choosing open land to settle them; ten stockades were placed and it was still named Xingtang County.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu raided Ding, took Xingtang, and relocated the entire populace north to Tan Prefecture on open ground; ten stockades were founded and the name Xingtang kept.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhangmin Palace.
translations.idiomatic: It answered to Zhangmin Palace.

translations.literal: Three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Fanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Zhuo County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Zhuo County.

translations.literal: Mid-Tang Wude era changed to Fanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-Tang Wude it was renamed Fanyang County.

translations.literal: There are Zhuo River and Fan River.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuo and Fan rivers flow there.

translations.literal: Ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Guan County.
translations.idiomatic: Guan County.

sentences.zh: 本漢方城縣，先屬廣陽國。

translations.literal: Originally Han Fangcheng County, first belonging to Guangyang State.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Fangcheng County in Guangyang State.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇九年，自易州淶水縣移置，屬幽州，取漢故安縣名。

translations.literal: Sui Kaihuang year 9 moved from Yizhou Laishui County to settle here, belonging to Youzhou, taking the Han Guan County name.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kaihuang year 9 moved the seat from Yizhou Laishui to Youzhou under the old Guan County name.

sentences.zh: 唐武德四年屬北義州，徙治章信堡。

translations.literal: Tang Wude year 4 belonged to Beiyi Prefecture and the seat moved to Zhangxin Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Wude year 4 it joined Beiyi Prefecture and the administration shifted to Zhangxin Fort.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年義州廢，移今治，復屬幽州。

translations.literal: Zhenguan year 2 Beiyi Prefecture abolished; moved to present administration and again belonged to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan year 2 abolished Beiyi and moved the seat here, again under Youzhou.

translations.literal: Ninety li southeast of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

translations.literal: Xincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Xinchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Xinchang County.

sentences.zh: 唐大歷四年析固安縣置，後省。

translations.literal: Tang Dali year 4 split off from Guan County to establish; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dali year 4 carved it from Guan County, then abolished it.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成四年復析范陽縣置，在州南六十里。
